question: I work full time here on a work permit and want my wife and our 10-year-old son to join me, but I rent a one-room flat. Is that a problem?
reference_answer: Not in itself. Family members of someone with a work permit are granted residence permits under 4 kap. 4 a § utlänningsförordningen, which requires that the person in Sweden can support themselves and the family members (exceptions for special reasons); it sets no requirement on the size of the home, so you do not need to move to a larger flat for that reason. The level: salary after preliminary tax of at least the protected amount for wage garnishment, counting the family members too (4 kap. 4 c §); Migrationsverket counts housing costs in this. The requirement of a home of sufficient size and standard (5 kap. 3 j § utlänningslagen) applies to other family cases, e.g. when the person in Sweden has or applies for permanent residence at the same time as the family.
notes: Situational (phase 5): the answer turns on which rule applies, which the question doesn't name. A trap: 5 kap. 3 j § (housing size) looks relevant but does not apply to a work-permit holder's family. Legal basis checked 2026-11-24: a work-permit holder's family is granted permits under 4 kap. 4 a § utlänningsförordningen (maintenance requirement, level in 4 c §, no housing-size requirement, same validity as the worker's permit), not 5 kap. 3 a § / 3 j § utlänningslagen. Reviewed 2026-11-24 on the review page. Review: OK; added that there is no need to move for a size requirement. 5 kap. 3 j § stays out of the expected sources on purpose: avoiding it is what the item tests.

question: My husband came here on a family permit tied to my work permit, which is valid until March 2027. How long is his permit valid?
reference_answer: Normally for the same period as your work permit, so until March 2027, but never for longer than his own passport is valid: a family member's permit granted under 4 kap. 4 a § utlänningsförordningen is valid for the same time as the permit of the person they are tied to (tredje stycket), and Migrationsverket's page adds the passport limit. Check the end date in his own permit decision. When you extend your permit he has to apply to extend his; it does not happen automatically.
notes: Situational (phase 5): the length is in the ordinance, which plain RAG rarely retrieves. Legal basis checked 2026-11-24: a work-permit holder's family is granted permits under 4 kap. 4 a § utlänningsförordningen (maintenance requirement, level in 4 c §, no housing-size requirement, same validity as the worker's permit), not 5 kap. 3 a § / 3 j § utlänningslagen. Reviewed 2026-11-24 on the review page. Review: added the passport limit (Migrationsverket's page, checked in the corpus), to check his own decision, and that an extension needs an application. Paragraph checked: the same-validity rule is the third paragraph in the wording in force from 2026-10-01 (the fourth in the 2025 wording). The page is not a required source.

question: I've had work permits for over four years, but I lost my job two months ago and live on unemployment benefit (a-kassa). Can I get permanent residence now?
reference_answer: The time requirement may be met (four years with a permit for work during the last seven, 5 kap. 5 § utlänningslagen), but permanent residence also requires that you can support yourself (5 kap. 7 § 1). Unemployment insurance benefits do not count: the requirement is a salary after preliminary tax of at least the protected amount for wage garnishment, or business income, with a certain permanence (4 kap. 4 e § utlänningsförordningen). So, while living on a-kassa, normally not; exceptions for special reasons are in 5 kap. 8 §. Permanent residence is normally applied for together with an extension of the work permit. Separately, the work permit itself may be revoked if you have no new job (or a new application that is later granted) within three months of the job ending (7 kap. 3 § första stycket 2); that is not automatic.
notes: Situational (phase 5): describes a situation without naming the rule; the target law section is one that no retrieved source cited in the failure analysis (2026-11-24). Targets 5 kap. 7 § and the ordinance's support level (4 kap. 4 e §). Reviewed 2026-11-24 on the review page. Review: OK; added that permanent residence is applied for with an extension and that revocation is not automatic.

question: My employer cut my salary below the work-permit requirement for a few months. Can my permit be revoked?
reference_answer: It can be. A temporary residence permit for work is to be revoked if the conditions for the work permit in 6 kap. 2 § första stycket, including the salary requirement, are no longer met for a reason other than the job ending (7 kap. 7 e § första stycket 1 utlänningslagen). It is not automatic: it need not be revoked in minor cases or where revocation would not be reasonable in the circumstances (tredje stycket), so how large the shortfall was, how long it lasted and why matter. Which salary level applied depends on when your permit was granted and the transitional rules, which the question does not say. A past shortfall can also lead to a refused extension later (6 kap. 4 a § andra stycket 4).
notes: Situational (phase 5): describes a situation without naming the rule; the target law section is one that no retrieved source cited in the failure analysis (2026-11-24). Target 7 kap. 7 e § (revocation when conditions lapse), with 6 kap. 2 § for the salary requirement. Review: which wording of 6 kap. 2 § the answer should name (80 or 90 percent depends on the grant date). Reviewed 2026-11-24 on the review page. Review: no fixed 80 or 90 percent threshold (it depends on dates the question does not give); revocation not automatic; size, duration and reasons matter; kept the extension warning.
